# User content and online safety

## Scope

Applies when the change touches content users post, upload, or send each other, and its moderation. Not when the product stores no content its users provide, and its users cannot reach each other. Neighbours: `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`, `aidd-team:products-for-children`, `aidd-team:ai-features`.

## Terms

- **Notice**: Anyone's report that a specific item is illegal, with its exact URL. An authority's removal order has a deadline instead.
- **Statement of reasons**: What a user is told when the service restricts their content or account: the measure, the facts, the ground, and the redress.
- **CyberTipline report**: A US provider's report of apparent child sexual exploitation to NCMEC. It starts a one-year preservation.
- **Designated agent**: The contact a US service registers for copyright notices. The safe harbor needs one.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2022-06-07 | EU: a hosting service removes terrorist content in every Member State within one hour of a removal order, and keeps it six months. | S8 |
| 2024-02-17 | EU: the DSA applies in full: notices, statements of reasons, suspected crime reports, complaints, trusted flaggers, and misuse. | S1, S2 |
| 2024-05-07 | US: a CyberTipline report preserves its contents for 1 year, and child sex trafficking is reported too. | S5 |
| 2025-03-17 | UK: Ofcom enforces the illegal content duties; each service's risk assessment was due 2025-03-16. | S3 |
| 2026-04-07 | UK: a user-to-user service reports CSEA content to the NCA when no NCMEC report covers it. | S6 |
| 2026-05-19 | US: a covered platform runs a notice and removal process for intimate images, and removes a valid request's image within 48 hours. | S4 |

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| Every restriction of a user's content or account gets a statement of reasons, however it was imposed: a notice, a filter, or a moderator. | A filter that hides or demotes a post and tells its author nothing. |
| A notifier gets a receipt, then the decision and the redress. A notice of child sexual abuse needs no name or email. | A report form that requires an account, or never answers the reporter. |
| A removal deadline runs from receipt: one hour for an EU removal order, 24 hours for an eSafety removal notice, 48 hours for a valid intimate image request. | A review queue that a weekend or a time zone holds past the deadline. |
| Apparent child sexual exploitation goes to NCMEC as soon as reasonably possible, and in the EU a threat to someone's life goes to the police. | A moderation flow that only deletes it, so nothing is reported or kept. |
| Reported or removed material is kept for its period, securely and with narrow access. | An account deletion or a retention job that erases what a report preserved. |
| On an online platform past micro or small size, a user can complain for six months after a decision, and qualified staff decide it, not only a model. | An appeal decided by the same classifier that made the first decision. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd risk --paths`) | Name each market, and whether the product is a hosting service, an online platform, or a covered platform. The author declares a change to removal, reporting, or preservation major. In the UK, it refreshes the illegal content risk assessment first. | S1, S4, S3 |
| Specify | The notice form takes the exact URL, the reason, the notifier's name and email, and a good-faith statement. It sends a receipt, then the decision with the redress. | S1 |
| Specify | Each restriction, from demotion to a suspension, sends a statement of reasons, which an online platform also files in the Commission's database. | S1, S2 |
| Specify | Each removal path has an owner and its deadline from receipt, and covers the item's known copies. | S8, S7, S4 |
| Specify | US copyright notices go to the designated agent. A counter notification restores the item in 10 to 14 business days, and repeat infringers lose their accounts. | S9 |
| Implement | Apparent child sexual exploitation goes to NCMEC's CyberTipline as soon as reasonably possible, or to the NCA for the UK when no NCMEC report covers it. The flow reports and preserves, never only deletes. | S5, S6 |
| Implement | Preserved material outlives account deletion and retention jobs, and only the staff who must can open it. | S5, S8 |
| Implement | Trusted flaggers' notices go first, and qualified staff decide complaints. A user who often posts manifestly illegal content, or files manifestly unfounded notices, is suspended after a warning. | S1, S2 |
| Roll out | Observe requests past their deadline, open complaints, and failed CyberTipline or database submissions. | S4, S5, S2 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Removal deadline test | each removal path meets its deadline from receipt, also at night and on a weekend | a fake clock, with each removal path checked at its deadline | S8, S7, S4 |
| Notice to decision test | a notice gets a receipt, then a decision the notifier hears, and every restriction, from a notice, a filter, or a moderator, sends a statement of reasons | end to end from the report button, and over each restriction | S1 |
| Preservation hold test | reported or removed material survives account deletion and retention jobs for its period, and only allowed staff open it | report an item, delete its account, run retention, then check the hold | S5, S8 |
| Abuse report routing test | apparent child sexual exploitation is reported and preserved, and its notice needs no name | a stub of each reporting API: an anonymous notice, a moderator's finding, and an automated match | S5, S1 |

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
